body.statement: For every compatible \(p\), dose \(d\), and endpoint in \(\{\underline\theta_d(p),\overline\theta_d(p)\}\), there exists \(q^\star\in\Gamma_L(p)\) attaining that endpoint with \(|\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)|\le3L-2\). For rational \(p\), one can construct \(q^\star\) with rational masses from the active facet certificate and complementary slackness. The support bound is uniformly sharp: at \(L=2\) with \(p_{0,1}=p_{1,1}=p_{2,1}=1/2\), the unique optimizer attaining \(\overline\theta_1(p)=1/4\) assigns mass \(1/4\) to each of \(001,010,100,111\), and therefore has support \(4=3L-2\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(L\ge 2\), a compatible marginal vector \(p\), a dose \(d\in\mathcal D\), and either the lower- or upper-endpoint objective.  The first step is a finite-support elimination argument, proved directly here.  Index columns by \(u\in\mathcal U_L\), and let \(M\) be the \((3L-2)\)-by-\(|\mathcal U_L|\) matrix with one row indexed by \(\varnothing\) and the remaining rows indexed by \((r,j)\in\mathcal D\times\{1,\ldots,L-1\}\), where
\[
 M_{\varnothing,u}=1,
 \qquad
 M_{(r,j),u}=\mathbf 1\{u_r=j\}.
\]
Set
\[
 b(p)=\bigl(1,(p_{rj})_{r\in\mathcal D,\,1\le j<L}\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The definition \(\text{def:coupling-fiber}\) gives
\[
 \Gamma_L(p)=\{q\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal U_L}:Mq=b(p)\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, every \(q\in\Gamma_L(p)\) satisfies these equations.  Conversely, if \(q\ge0\) and \(Mq=b(p)\), then the first row gives \(\sum_u q(u)=1\), while for each \(r\in\mathcal D\) the omitted level-zero equation follows from
\[
 \sum_{u:u_r=0}q(u)
 =1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\sum_{u:u_r=j}q(u)
 =1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}p_{rj}
 =p_{r0}.
\]
The last equality uses the stated condition that each arm marginal \((p_{rj})_{j\in\mathcal Y_L}\) is a probability vector.  This proves (1).

Compatibility means that the set in (1) is nonempty.  It is closed and contained in the finite probability simplex, hence compact.  By \(\text{def:unique-peak-indicators}\),
\[
 q\longmapsto\theta_d(q)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}B_d(u)q(u)
\]
is linear and continuous, so it attains its minimum and maximum on \(\Gamma_L(p)\).

For either objective, choose an optimizer \(q^\star\) with minimum support, and put \(S=\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)\).  Suppose that the columns \((M_u)_{u\in S}\) were linearly dependent.  Then there would be a nonzero vector \(z\), supported on \(S\), with \(Mz=0\).  Since \(q^\star(u)>0\) for \(u\in S\), both \(q^\star+\varepsilon z\) and \(q^\star-\varepsilon z\) are nonnegative for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), and (1) makes both feasible.  For a minimum, both perturbed objective values are at least the optimum; for a maximum, both are at most the optimum.  Their average is the objective value at \(q^\star\), so in either case both are optimal and
\[
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}B_d(u)z(u)=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
The mass row of \(Mz=0\) gives \(\sum_u z(u)=0\), so nonzero \(z\) has both signs.  Therefore
\[
 t=\min_{u\in S:z(u)<0}\frac{q^\star(u)}{-z(u)}>0
\]
makes \(q^\star+tz\) feasible, optimal by (2), and supported on a strict subset of \(S\), a contradiction.  Thus the columns indexed by \(S\) are linearly independent, and the explicit row count yields
\[
 |\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)|
 \le \operatorname{rank}(M)
 \le 3L-2.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next give the promised construction from an active facet certificate; this is a nonnegative-slack complementary-slackness argument.  For \(h_i\in\mathcal H_L\), write its inequality as
\[
 a_i(p)+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}\theta\ge0,
 \qquad
 a_i(p)=\kappa_i+
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\alpha_{irj}p_{rj}.
\]
For every \(q\in\Gamma_L(p)\), equations (1), the definition of \(\theta(q)\), and \(\text{def:canonical-facet-set}\) give the exact expectation identity
\[
 a_i(p)+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}\theta(q)
 =\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q(u)\ge0,
 \tag{4}
\]
because \(s_{h_i}(u)\ge0\) on the legal support \(\mathcal U_L\).

For a lower endpoint, \(\text{thm:sharp-three-facet-endpoints}\) supplies an attaining \(\lambda\in\mathcal D_d^-\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i=e_d,
 \qquad
 \underline\theta_d(p)=-\sum_i\lambda_i a_i(p),
 \qquad
 \lambda_i\ge0.
 \tag{5}
\]
Applying (4) to any lower-endpoint optimizer gives
\[
 0=\underline\theta_d(p)+\sum_i\lambda_i a_i(p)
 =\sum_i\lambda_i\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q^\star(u).
 \tag{6}
\]
All terms are nonnegative, so \(\lambda_i>0\) and \(q^\star(u)>0\) imply \(s_{h_i}(u)=0\).  For an upper endpoint, the same theorem supplies an attaining \(\mu\in\mathcal D_d^+\) with
\[
 \sum_i\mu_i\beta_i=-e_d,
 \qquad
 \overline\theta_d(p)=\sum_i\mu_i a_i(p),
 \qquad
 \mu_i\ge0,
 \tag{7}
\]
and (4) yields
\[
 0=\sum_i\mu_i a_i(p)-\overline\theta_d(p)
 =\sum_i\mu_i\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q^\star(u).
 \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(\mu_i>0\) and \(q^\star(u)>0\) likewise imply \(s_{h_i}(u)=0\).

Let \(\rho\) denote the active certificate, either \(\lambda\) or \(\mu\), and define its common tight set by
\[
 T_\rho=\{u\in\mathcal U_L:s_{h_i}(u)=0
 \text{ for every }i\text{ with }\rho_i>0\}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Equations (6) and (8) show that
\[
 M_{T_\rho}q_{T_\rho}=b(p),
 \qquad q_{T_\rho}\ge0
 \tag{10}
\]
is nonempty.  Conversely, extend any solution of (10) by zero outside \(T_\rho\).  It belongs to \(\Gamma_L(p)\) by (1).  Summing (4) with the certificate weights gives equality in (5) or (7), so the extension attains the specified endpoint.  Applying the preceding support-elimination argument within (10) gives a solution supported on at most \(3L-2\) legal response types.

This also gives a finite exact construction.  Enumerate subsets \(S\subseteq T_\rho\) with \(|S|\le3L-2\), solve
\[
 M_Sq_S=b(p),\qquad q_S\ge0,
 \tag{11}
\]
and accept the first solution whose columns \(M_S\) are linearly independent.  Nonemptiness of (10) and the elimination proof guarantee success.  If \(p\) is rational, then \(b(p)\) is rational and all entries of \(M\) are integers.  Moreover, on the linearly independent support of an active certificate, the equations \(\sum_i\rho_i\beta_i=\pm e_d\) have a unique solution and a nonsingular integer minor, so the certificate weights are rational.  The tight set (9) is therefore exactly decidable using the integral slacks.  For an accepted support \(S\), choose \(|S|\) rows \(R\) for which the square integer matrix \(M_{R,S}\) is nonsingular.  Then
\[
 q_S=M_{R,S}^{-1}b_R(p)
\]
is rational; rational Gaussian elimination verifies the remaining equations and nonnegativity in (11).  Hence the active certificate and complementary slackness construct an endpoint-attaining mixture with rational masses.

Finally, the support cap in (3) is uniformly sharp in the sense required for an all-\(L\) guarantee.  Take \(L=2\) and \(p_{0,1}=p_{1,1}=p_{2,1}=1/2\).  By \(\text{def:non-valley-support}\), the only deleted binary triple is \(101\).  Write \(x_{abc}=q(a,b,c)\) for the seven legal triples.  The three level-one marginal equations are
\[
 x_{100}+x_{110}+x_{111}=\frac12,
 \quad
 x_{010}+x_{011}+x_{110}+x_{111}=\frac12,
 \quad
 x_{001}+x_{011}+x_{111}=\frac12.
 \tag{12}
\]
Combining (12) with \(\sum x_{abc}=1\) gives
\[
 x_{000}=x_{111}-x_{010}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Nonnegativity therefore implies \(x_{111}\ge x_{010}\).  By \(\text{def:unique-peak-indicators}\), \(B_1(u)=1\) only at \(u=010\), so \(\theta_1(q)=x_{010}\).  The middle equation in (12) and (13) yield
\[
 \frac12=x_{010}+x_{011}+x_{110}+x_{111}
 \ge2x_{010},
\]
and hence \(\overline\theta_1(p)\le1/4\).  The mixture
\[
 x_{001}=x_{010}=x_{100}=x_{111}=\frac14,
 \qquad
 x_{000}=x_{011}=x_{110}=0
 \tag{14}
\]
is supported on legal triples, satisfies all three marginals in (12), and has \(\theta_1=1/4\).  Thus \(\overline\theta_1(p)=1/4\).  If equality holds, then (12)--(13) force \(x_{111}=x_{010}=1/4\) and \(x_{011}=x_{110}=0\); the first and third equations in (12) then force \(x_{100}=x_{001}=1/4\), while (13) forces \(x_{000}=0\).  Therefore (14) is the unique optimizer, and every optimizer has support \(4=3L-2\).  In particular, the universal support guarantee cannot be reduced to \(3L-3\).  No division by an unknown probability, treatment-overlap argument, boundary limit, or asymptotic condition is used; the proof uses only finite \(L\), compatible arm-probability vectors, nonnegative masses on \(\mathcal U_L\), and the declared facet theorem.
body.justification: Sharpness requires compatible response-triple laws, not only valid dual inequalities.
body.gap: Two-way constructive tables are available in LuDingDasgupta2018; the present construction must honor a forbidden three-way support at every endpoint branch.
body.consumer: Endpoint-attaining mixtures provide transparent worst-case response profiles for benefit-risk reporting and sensitivity analysis.
